newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: South African wool prices fall at weekly sale.
newsitem.headline: South African wool prices fall at weekly sale.

text.p: South African wool prices fell at the latest weekly auction, the Wool Board said on Thursday.
Of the total 7,579 bales on offer, 94.7 percent was sold.
Prices for 20 micron dropped 2.3 percent, 21 fell 2.4 percent, 22 lost 4.1 pct, 23 slipped 8.6 percent, 24 micron downed 6.0 percent and 25 micron slid 2.7 percent.
Bellies fell 3.0 percent, lambs clipped 1.2 percent and locks cut 5.7 percent.
The offering included 1,643 bales of merino bellies, lambs and locks together with 990 other white, 705 bales Lesotho and 340 bales of coarse and coloured.
Top-selling wool was 21 micron which sold 93.7 pct of 1,204 bales.
536 bales offered and 87.5 percent of 20 micron sold.
1,037 bales offered and 92.1 percent of 22 micron sold.
428 bales offered and 84.4 percent of 23 micron sold.
171 bales offered and 89.5 percent of 24 micron sold.
42 bales offered and 73.8 percent of 25 micron were sold.
The next sale will be held on February 12 with about 10,000 bales on offer.
